note: Fact base for the Cognition.X Trades Network: 37 trade families crossed with 6 regions = 222 regional union/trade entries (San Francisco, Oakland–East Bay, Los Angeles on the West Coast; New Orleans, Baton Rouge–River Region, Houston–Gulf Coast on the Gulf). International union names are real and public; LOCAL/CHAPTER NUMBERS ARE DELIBERATELY NOT LISTED — locals merge, renumber and redistrict, so every entry carries the same instruction: verify the current local with the regional building-trades or labor council before publishing. Simulation scenarios are training exercises phrased against real, publicly known sites; they teach control discipline and observation and never count as equipment certification or union credit. Each family also carries a classroom hook — the school subjects it teaches through (math, science, ELA, civics) and one concrete in-class connection — feeding the Trades Across School Subjects pack.

families.sim: Trace a de-energized circuit from panel to device at {site}, narrating lockout-tagout at every step
families.school: Ohm's law as ratio and proportion; series vs. parallel circuits with battery and bulb.

families.intl: International Brotherhood of Electrical Workers (IBEW, utility branch)
families.sim: Walk a storm-restoration switching order for {site} on paper, with the feeder map open and every hold point named
families.school: The grid as a system diagram; who restores power after a storm and in what order.

families.sim: Chart supply, waste and vent for one fixture group serving {site}, then pressure-test the logic against the code table
families.school: Water pressure, gravity and the siphon; pipe volume and flow-rate arithmetic.

families.sim: Read an isometric spool drawing for a run at {site} and stage its fit-up sequence with tack points called in order
families.school: Reading isometric drawings; thermal expansion measured on a heated rod.

families.sim: Lay out sprinkler coverage for one floor plan drawn from {site}, then defend head spacing against the obstruction rules
families.school: Coverage circles and spacing on a floor plan — geometry with lives attached.

families.sim: Frame a scale wall section matched to details from {site} — layout, plumb, square — and hand a punch list to a partner
families.school: Fractions on the tape measure; the 3-4-5 triangle that squares every corner.

families.intl: United Brotherhood of Carpenters (UBC, millwright division)
families.sim: Level and align a motor-to-pump train on the bench as if installed at {site}, logging shim moves to the thousandth
families.school: Alignment to the thousandth — tolerance, precision and measurement error made real.

families.intl: United Brotherhood of Carpenters (UBC, pile drivers)
families.sim: Model bearing versus friction piles in a sand box for ground like {site}, and read refusal from the blow count
families.school: Bearing vs. friction in a sand-box model; why the blow count is data.

families.sim: Run a crane-simulator lift plan sized from {site}: pick radius, load chart, and the one call that stops the lift
families.school: The load chart as a function of radius; the pendulum physics of a swinging load.

families.sim: Sequence steel erection for a bay of {site} — columns, beams, plumb-up — and name the connection each bolt-up needs
families.school: Triangles and bracing — why the truss holds; load paths traced through a frame.

families.sim: Plan trench protection for a utility cut near {site}: soil class, shoring choice, and the flagged line that stops the dig
families.school: Soil types and trench physics; the flagged utility line as public safety in the ground.

families.sim: Develop the flat pattern for a duct transition serving {site}, cut it in paper, and prove the fit by folding
families.school: Flat-pattern development — 3-D shapes unfolded into 2-D geometry you can cut and fold.

families.intl: International Union of Painters and Allied Trades (IUPAT)
families.sim: Write the surface-prep and coating schedule for an exposure like {site}, and justify each coat by what it stops
families.school: Area take-offs for coverage; why coatings cure — evaporation vs. chemical change.

families.sim: Plan a curtain-wall lite replacement at {site} on paper: glass handling, suction rig checks, and the wind call
families.school: Wind load on a pane; thermal breaks and why glass and metal move differently.

families.sim: Take one wall from board to level-4 finish in a classroom mock-up matched to {site}, logging coats and dry times
families.school: Plaster's chemistry — hydration, working time and the cure you can watch.

families.sim: Pour, screed and finish a slab sample as specified for {site}, and read the bull-float window from the sheen
families.school: Concrete as chemistry with a clock; mix ratios scaled like recipes.

families.intl: International Union of Bricklayers and Allied Craftworkers (BAC)
families.sim: Lay a sample lead corner to a story pole drawn from {site}, keeping bond, level and plumb through six courses
families.school: Bond patterns, courses and the story pole — modular arithmetic on a wall.

families.intl: United Union of Roofers, Waterproofers and Allied Workers
families.sim: Detail the flashing at a wall-to-deck transition like {site}'s, and trace the water path that proves it dry
families.school: Slope as rise over run; tracing the water path that proves a detail dry.

families.intl: International Association of Heat and Frost Insulators
families.sim: Size insulation for a chilled and a steam line at {site} and show the condensation math that picks the thickness
families.school: Conduction, convection, radiation — R-value as measurable insulation math.

families.sim: Walk a confined-space entry plan for a vessel at {site}: permits, attendant, atmosphere checks, retrieval
families.school: Pressure, temperature and the confined-space atmosphere — gas laws with rules attached.

families.sim: Map the safety chain of a traction elevator serving {site} — governor, safeties, buffers — and what trips each
families.school: Counterweights and mechanical advantage; the safety chain as an engineered system.

families.sim: Plan a permitted oversize delivery to {site}: route survey, escort points, and the hour the city allows the move
families.school: Route, weight and time arithmetic; who permits an oversize load through a city.

families.sim: Choreograph one container move at {site} — crane, hostler, stack — and call the pinch points a walker must never cross
families.school: Container arithmetic at port scale; how trade through one wharf shapes a region's history.

families.sim: Take a worn part from {site} from measurement to process plan: datum, tolerance, and the machine that holds it
families.school: Datum, tolerance and measurement — decimals to the thousandth on real parts.

families.sim: Design the fiber path from street cabinet to classroom for {site}, and test-plan every splice you drew
families.school: Light down a fiber; bandwidth and signal loss as rates and ratios.

families.sim: Run a blocking diagram for {site} through one service day, and recover the schedule after a simulated 20-minute gap
families.school: Headways and schedules as rate problems; transit as a public service the city votes on.

families.sim: Work a switching problem in a yard modeled on {site}: moves, shove protection, and the three-step protection rule
families.school: Switching puzzles as logic problems; momentum and stopping distance at train scale.

families.sim: Stand a simulated engine-room watch for a vessel working {site}: log readings, catch the one drifting gauge
families.school: The engine-room watch as data logging — reading gauges and catching the drift.

families.sim: Plan and narrate a mooring evolution at {site}: line order, winch commands, and the snap-back zones nobody stands in
families.school: Lines under load — force, snap-back and why geometry keeps a deck crew alive.

families.sim: Build a pre-incident plan for {site}: access, water supply, hazards, and the first-alarm assignment that fits it
families.school: Fire triangle and water supply math; how a city plans its own protection.

families.sim: Produce the rigging plot and load-in schedule for {site}, with every point's weight and the show-stop authority named
families.school: Rigging plots — point loads, angles and the arithmetic hanging over the stage.

families.sim: Run a banquet line simulation scaled to {site}: mise en place, allergy chain of custody, and the 200-cover clock
families.school: Scaling recipes as ratios; heat, time and food safety as applied chemistry.

families.sim: Trace cold chain from dock to case for a store serving {site}'s neighborhood, and log the two temperature gates
families.school: Cold-chain temperatures as data; inventory arithmetic from dock to shelf.

families.sim: Prioritize one storm's work orders for the crews serving {site} — trees, drains, signals — and defend the triage
families.school: Work orders and triage after a storm — the civics of who fixes what first.

families.sim: Co-plan one flipped trades lesson with a union mentor for {site}: the at-home watch, the in-class build, the check
families.school: The flipped lesson itself as a text — writing directions that cannot be misread.

families.sim: Walk the plant of {site} with its custodial and food-service leads and chart one day's unseen work as a system
families.school: A school's plant as a living system — mapping one day of unseen work.

families.sim: Contract, rehearse and run a three-tune set for {site} on union terms: the call, the book, the split, the encore
families.school: Time signatures and rhythm as fractions; the union contract as a working document.
